deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This argument controls whether Terraform can destroy the resource. The default value of DELETE allows unrestricted destructive operations. A generic platform policy can require this to be set to PREVENT, blocking accidental or unauthorized deletion of the security profile via terraform destroy or terraform apply. This enforces a deletion-blocking safeguard across all teams without requiring team-specific values, preventing destructive loss of cloud resources at the platform level.

description.rationale: This is free-text informational metadata describing the security profile. It has no effect on which assessments are run, how they are weighted, or how the profile behaves. Constraining it would not improve security posture.

org_id.description:
The Apigee Organization associated with the Apigee Security Profile V2,
in the format 'organizations/{{org_name}}'.
org_id.rationale: This is a reference to the parent Apigee Organization. The value is inherently team- or project-specific (the organization name). A generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding specific organization identifiers. The security of the organization itself is governed by the google_apigee_organization resource, not by resources that reference it.

profile_id.description: Resource ID of the security profile.
profile_id.rationale: This is the naming identifier for the security profile. The chosen name has no effect on what the profile assesses or how it scores findings. A naming policy would be organizational preference, not a security control.

profile_assessment_configs.description: A map of the assessment name and the assessment config.

profile_assessment_configs.assessment.description: The identifier for this object. Format specified above.
profile_assessment_configs.assessment.rationale: This identifies which security assessment check this entry configures (e.g. auth-policies-check, threat-policies-check). Which assessments a team includes depends on their API architecture and security requirements. A per-entry policy cannot enforce that certain assessments must be present across the entire profile; it can only constrain individual entry values. The choice of which checks to include is a team-level architectural decision.

profile_assessment_configs.weight.description: The weight of the assessment. Possible values: ["MINOR", "MODERATE", "MAJOR"]
profile_assessment_configs.weight.rationale: This determines how significant a security assessment check is in the overall risk score. Per GCP documentation, weights translate to point values: MINOR = 1, MODERATE = 5, MAJOR = 15. Setting a check to MINOR effectively neuters its impact on the security score, meaning a failure barely registers and is unlikely to drive remediation. A generic platform policy can blacklist MINOR to ensure all included security assessments carry meaningful weight (at least MODERATE), preventing teams from undermining the purpose of their security profile by downplaying findings. No team-specific values are needed.
